title: fix(models): honor explicit catalog refresh budgets
body:
## What Problem This Solves

An explicit model-catalog refresh already admits a 180-second acquisition, but the shared HTTP acquisition helpers still default to five seconds. A healthy slow discovery can therefore appear unavailable before the existing refresh budget expires.

Related: #168356 and [Homelab #1992](https://github.com/jlapenna/homelab/issues/1992). This fixes propagation of the existing budget; it does not add a configuration option or close the broader runtime-adoption request.

## User Impact

Explicit refreshes can use their existing admitted budget. Ordinary discovery retains its five-second limit, and an explicitly tighter HTTP timeout remains binding. Existing zero-timeout meanings are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the admitted deadline through the existing catalog-expiry context and HTTP helpers. Separate pending loads by their stable effective budget while continuing to share healthy completed values with their original TTL. Preserve shared-load cancellation/cache warming, generation ownership, auth, SSRF protection, pagination and body limits.

This is separate from the held diagnostics PR #165915. Both touch implicit-provider discovery and its scope tests; that branch and its diagnostics changes remain untouched.

## Evidence

- Before the implementation, the admitted-budget regression passed the ordinary-budget control and failed the explicit-refresh case on base 2ce02afe77cffc9ce4e9ba62f0c76c3dadebe7a8.
- The strengthened regression advances a fake transport six seconds through the real implicit owner and acquisition helper: ordinary discovery remains unavailable while the explicit refresh returns healthy rows. No real provider/model request or wall-clock sleep is used.
- Final focused verification: **82 tests passed across seven files/four shards**, covering discovery scope, shared cache/runtime/upstream feed, the shared-upstream contract and representative Nvidia/OpenRouter consumers. Earlier focused cancellation, eviction, cache-warming and TTL controls also passed.
- Final format and typed oxlint checks on all eight changed files, core typecheck, SDK export/surface checks, plugin-boundary check, changed-file line-cap check and normal commit hooks passed.
- The optional whole-tree max-lines ratchet fails on three unchanged base files: ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx, ui/src/pages/config/config-page-state.ts and ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page-state.ts. Their bytes and the checker/baseline are unchanged by this PR.
- Independent source reviews covered deadline propagation, pending-budget isolation, freshness ownership and zero-timeout compatibility. Exact-head upstream CI39251502431 completed successfully; no deployed Gateway/runtime adoption or UI success is claimed.

All setup, tests and checks ran in serialized native services capped at one CPU, 6 GiB RAM, zero swap and 512 tasks. The initial focused-check phase's largest observed memory peak was 5.2 GiB.

## Real guarded-HTTP refresh proof (2026-10-19)

At unchanged head `7bd6a4ad95fa3e048f179edb01db9f0e54891850`, an isolated real HTTP fixture exercised the production `prepareAgentCatalogSource(..., "live", false, {refresh:true, providerDiscoveryTimeoutMs:180000})` acquisition entry used by the prepared-catalog worker. The provider was loaded through the normal manifest/provider-catalog entry path and called the public SDK helper with the default production `fetchWithSsrFGuard`. No fake clock, mocked fetch/guard, injected fetch implementation or leaf-timeout override was used.

The owned local server waited a real six seconds before sending HTTP200 and its model row. That row was absent from configured/static models. The normal endpoint-derived hostname policy and fixture-scoped HTTP allowance were used; no global SSRF policy changed. The process started with `env -i`, private HOME/config/state/cache, empty auth profiles and only the fixture plugin enabled; it made no live provider/model request.

Sanitized terminal results from the normal node invocation:

```json
{"head":"7bd6a4ad95fa3e048f179edb01db9f0e54891850","entrypoint":"prepareAgentCatalogSource","refresh":true,"transport":"default fetchWithSsrFGuard","timeoutMs":180000,"elapsedMs":6457,"responseElapsedMs":6002,"requests":1,"served":1,"returnedModelIds":["slow-http-only-model"],"outcomes":[],"status":"PASS"}
{"head":"7bd6a4ad95fa3e048f179edb01db9f0e54891850","entrypoint":"prepareAgentCatalogSource","refresh":true,"transport":"default fetchWithSsrFGuard","timeoutMs":5000,"elapsedMs":5064,"responseElapsedMs":null,"requests":1,"served":0,"returnedModelIds":[],"outcomes":[{"provider":"proof-local-5000","status":"unavailable"}],"status":"PASS"}
```

The tighter-budget control emitted the real guarded-client timeout after4999ms (elapsed5000ms). It used the same refresh acquisition entry with a5000ms admitted budget and a separate fixture/cache context; it is not claimed as a complete ordinary CLI/Gateway lifecycle test. Both cases required an actual server request. The180000ms case returned the HTTP-only row after6.457s; the5000ms case returned no row before the delayed response could be served.

The native capped unit ran12:52:37–12:53:20 UTC and exited0, with systemd-reported43.432s wall time,28.488s CPU and824.7M memory peak. Its recorded command verified the unchanged clean Git head and reviewed ephemeral fixture SHA256 `fd52b42d60061260bbcfe179b1b75ce8453b05caedbb0ed6d84f1ee57b212ff2` before execution. All local response timers/sockets closed. The guarded task checkout, fixture/plugin/state/cache and owned units were removed by12:54:28; no tracked source change or permanent harness was added.

This proves real production-client acquisition at the explicit-refresh boundary. It does not claim deployed Gateway publication, UI acceptance or managed runtime adoption.
